result: I concluded that the structure is disordered: the phenyl ring of the cation sits in two tilted orientations, and I submitted that model. The evidence was in the displacement parameters, not the difference map. The largest peak was only 0.28 e/Å³, but ring atoms C2 and C3 had very elongated ellipsoids (U22 about 0.22 Å², anisotropy ratios of 6.4 and 7.4), all stretched perpendicular to the ring plane. I first split only C2/C3, then the whole ring, keeping C1 shared. Each version improved the fit: R1 fell from 0.0518 to 0.0483 and wR2 from 0.1255 to 0.1190, at a cost of 46 extra parameters. In the final model the two orientations (C2A–C6A in PART 1 and C2B–C6B in PART 2) are tilted in opposite directions, separated by about 0.7 Å at C2/C3. Their occupancies refined to 0.634/0.366 on one free variable, and each part has its own riding hydrogens. I held each ring flat and hexagonal with SADI and FLAT restraints, and kept the displacement parameters sensible with SIMU and a RIGU on C4A/C4B. All split atoms now have normal ellipsoids (anisotropy 2.1–3.5), and the residual map stays flat (maximum 0.25 e/Å³). I left the rest of the model unchanged. The piperazinium carbons are still somewhat elongated (ratios around 3–3.5), but nothing there pointed to resolvable disorder.
